scenario.description: A chief legal officer must decide whether to approve the current proposed patent license to HelioGrid and finalize the terms of any counterproposal, including territory, field of use, royalty, exclusivity, and sublicensing, with input from patent counsel and the technology licensing lead.

shared_context.S1: The company has developed a battery-management technology covered by a portfolio of issued patents.
shared_context.S2: Maya Chen sets the final decision on whether to approve the current HelioGrid draft as submitted.
shared_context.S3: HelioGrid has proposed a ten-year worldwide exclusive license with a 5% royalty on net sales and unrestricted sublicensing.
shared_context.S4: The proposed license is intended to support HelioGrid's commercial deployment of the technology.
shared_context.S5: HelioGrid has requested execution by June 30 to align with its planned commercial launch, and no license has been signed.
shared_context.S6: Under the firm's standard pre-execution review, patent counsel and the technology licensing lead report their findings before Maya makes the final decision.

PF1.text: Thomas reviewed the latest patent-maintenance records and confirmed that enforceable portfolio coverage for this license currently exists only in the United States and Germany; he also confirmed that the maintenance fee for US Patent 11-482901 is due in 9 days. He retrieved these records after the draft was circulated and has not yet added them to the patent schedule. Because the decision concerns approval of the current draft as submitted, these findings require approve_license to be false: Maya must withhold approval of that draft and counter with corrected terms, rather than approve the draft merely because a revised license could later be prepared.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed in a call with HelioGrid's commercial sponsor that the approved business term sheet permits exclusivity only for grid-scale battery storage, sets the royalty at exactly 6% of net sales, and prohibits sublicensing; HelioGrid will not sign on the broader draft terms. She has not entered the call terms into the deal tracker yet.

acceptance_conditions: The proposed draft must not be approved as written because its worldwide scope exceeds current enforceable patent coverage.
The licensed territories must be exactly the United States and Germany.
The settlement must include a commitment to pay the maintenance fee for US Patent 11-482901 within 9 days.
Exclusivity must be limited to grid-scale battery storage.
The royalty must be exactly 6% of net sales.
The patent-coverage finding must be cited as justification.
The approved business-term finding must be formally revealed and cited as justification.

content_checks.C3: any((('11-482901' in c['detail']) or ('maintenance fee' in c['detail'])) and (('9 days' in c['detail']) or ('within 9 days' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: decisions['exclusive_field_of_use'] == 'grid-scale battery storage' or decisions['exclusive_field_of_use'] == 'grid-scale battery storage applications' or decisions['exclusive_field_of_use'] == 'grid-scale battery storage uses'

decisive_facts.why: The patent-maintenance records change the decision on the current draft from approval to withholding approval, change the territory to exactly the United States and Germany, and require payment of the US Patent 11-482901 maintenance fee within 9 days.

The approved business term sheet changes the commercial package to exclusivity only for grid-scale battery storage, exactly 6% royalty, and no sublicensing, while requiring those terms to be formally disclosed and cited.
